evidence.summary: Candidate suite report says 90 tests passed, with expectations regenerated from rs-new.
Performance claim says the candidate is twice as fast but omits machine and workload details.
No old implementation, contract, old fixture, baseline observations, approvals or reproducible benchmark are provided.

checks.contract: No baseline contract or baseline observation is supplied for request {} timeout serialization or semantics.
checks.candidate: Candidate-only observation N1 reports {"timeout":null} for request {} at rs-new.

checks.contract: Parity requires an independent baseline oracle, such as an old contract, old fixture, baseline observation or unchanged expected output.
checks.candidate: The rs-new suite passed 90 tests, but expectations were regenerated from rs-new and therefore do not establish old-versus-new behavior preservation.

checks.contract: No reproducible benchmark workload, machine details or baseline measurement are supplied for the claimed speedup.
checks.candidate: P1 is a candidate-side performance claim only and does not provide enough conditions to compare or reproduce the result.

oracleRisks.reason: The reported passing suite regenerated expectations from the candidate, so it is not an independent oracle for migration parity.

nextTests.action: Provide the ts-old timeout contract or a captured ts-old run for request {} under specified session/default conditions, then run or capture rs-new under the same conditions.
nextTests.expected: The candidate timeout output can be classified only by comparing rs-new {"timeout":null} against an independent ts-old contract or observation.

nextTests.action: Restore expected outputs from ts-old or generate expected values from a baseline oracle rather than rs-new, then compare unchanged fixtures against rs-new.
nextTests.expected: A passing result should mean rs-new matches baseline-defined outputs; mismatches remain visible instead of being absorbed into regenerated expectations.

nextTests.action: Define the benchmark workload, machine/environment, sample size and baseline measurement before using performance as a bounded observation.
nextTests.expected: A performance comparison states the same workload and environment for ts-old and rs-new and reports reproducible measurements; it remains separate from correctness parity.

verdict.reason: The packet contains only candidate-side evidence, regenerated expectations and an unreproducible performance claim. With no independent baseline oracle or scoped approval, parity for the reviewed surfaces remains unknown.
